artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_2$ denote the field with two elements and for $r \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\mathbb{F}_2^r$ be the $r$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{F}_2$. For a finite subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^r$, define the sumset $A+A = \{a+a' : a, a' \in A\}$, and say that $A$ has doubling at most $K$ if $|A+A| \le K|A|$.

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that for every $K > 1$, every $r \in \mathbb{N}$, and every finite subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^r$ with $|A+A| \le K|A|$, there is a linear subspace $V \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^r$ satisfying
$$|V| \le K^c |A| \qquad \text{and} \qquad |A \cap V| \ge K^{-c}|A|?$$

Equivalently: is it true that every function $f: \mathbb{F}_2^r \to \mathbb{F}_2^\infty$ (where $\mathbb{F}_2^\infty$ is the countably infinite dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{F}_2$) can be written as the sum of a linear function and a function whose image has cardinality polynomially bounded in the cardinality of the set
$$\{f(x+y) + f(x) + f(y) : x, y \in \mathbb{F}_2^r\}?$$
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa (Marton) conjecture over $\mathbb{F}_2$. It was solved in November 2023 by Tim Gowers, Ben Green, Freddie Manners, and Terence Tao in the paper "On a conjecture of Marton" (arXiv:2311.05762), which establishes the conjecture in characteristic 2 with explicit polynomial bounds.
